description: We are MASTER CONTROL, a multidisciplinary team of passionate developers, builders, and problem-solvers participating in the Kumasi local event for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. With a strong foundation in software engineering, hardware prototyping, and data-driven artificial intelligence, we excel at the intersection of complex problem-solving and innovative technology.
summary:
On the way to Mars, a message to Earth can take up to 24 minutes each way, and the crew cannot come home quickly. NASA calls this problem Earth-Independent Medical Operations: when an astronaut feels unwell, the first response has to happen on board.

Sentinel is a voice-first health companion that runs on the spacecraft. A crew member says "Hey Sentinel". Sentinel reads their pulse from the camera, compares every reading with that person's own baseline, and shows the body system that changed on real 3D anatomy. It then explains in plain words what the change means and guides the next step. It also queues a summary for the flight surgeon so the delay doesn't hold up care.

Every medical decision comes from readable rules grounded in NASA data: 68 JSC 28913 Medical Requirements Integration Documents, NASA-STD-3001 limits, NASA DONKI and live NOAA space weather. A language model only phrases the answer, and Sentinel checks every number it says against the record. Sentinel works offline, labels each value LIVE, MANUAL or SIM, and speaks seven languages. It describes changes from baseline. It never diagnoses.
details:
Day 120 on the way to Mars. Eliah wakes up with a headache and blurry vision. A message to Earth takes up to 24 minutes each way, and the flight surgeon is asleep. What does Eliah do right now?

Eliah says: "Hey Sentinel, my head hurts."

That is the whole interface. Sentinel is an onboard health companion for deep-space crews, built for NASA's goal of Earth-Independent Medical Operations: when help from Earth is late, the first response has to happen on board.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT

1. Sentinel highlights the head on a 3D model of Eliah's body and records the symptom.

2. It reads Eliah's pulse and breathing from the tablet camera, with no wearable needed.

3. It compares every reading with Eliah's own normal, not an average person's.

4. It explains in plain words what changed, what to do now, and when to check again.

5. With one sentence ("send a summary to ground") it queues a report for the flight surgeon, ready for when the link is back.

WHY CREWS CAN TRUST IT

- Rules decide, AI only talks. Every alert comes from a readable rule with limits taken from NASA documents. The language model only phrases the answer, and every number it says is checked against the record first. It cannot invent a diagnosis.

- "Why this?" on every alert shows the rule and the NASA source behind it.

- Every number is labelled LIVE (measured), MANUAL (typed in) or SIM (simulated), so nobody mistakes a demo value for a real one.

- It keeps working offline and during a comms blackout.

BUILT FOR BUSY PEOPLE

Astronauts have no time to learn software. Sentinel is voice-first: talk to it, interrupt it, or tap. A new user taps Begin, picks their name and is in. A built-in Guide lists what to say ("I don't feel well", "show my body", "space weather", "start an EVA"), and the person can ask "what can I say?" at any time.

WHAT ELSE IT COVERS

- Radiation: live NOAA space weather, a shelter alert and a personal dose passport. The solar-storm drill replays a real event from NASA DONKI (May 2024).

- EVA: readiness check, suit monitoring and a leak alarm.

- Daily routine: check-in, reminders, a daily eye check for vision changes in space (SANS), cabin oxygen and CO2.

- Wellbeing: a breathing game driven by heart rate, a Mars greenhouse to tend, a private journal, and crew messages to fight isolation.

- Seven languages: English, Twi, Ewe, Ga, Fante, Dagbani and Yoruba.

USE OF NASA DATA

- 68 NASA Medical Requirements Integration Documents (JSC 28913), turned into structured data. They decide what Sentinel tracks, how each reading is taken and why it matters, and all 68 are listed in the app's Evidence screen.

- NASA-STD-3001 / OCHMO technical briefs: cabin CO2, oxygen and radiation limits.

- NASA DONKI solar energetic particle events, and 691 NASA Life Sciences Portal datasets mapped to Sentinel's health indicators.

IMPACT

For crews: a first response they can see the reasons for, in seconds, with no network. For the flight surgeon: organised summaries instead of raw data. On Earth, the same design fits remote clinics with no doctor nearby, which is why it speaks Ghanaian and Nigerian languages as well as English.

TOOLS

JavaScript, three.js and MediaPipe (front end, 3D anatomy, camera pulse); Python and FastAPI (rules engine and server); Supabase Postgres (encrypted crew record); Claude, Groq Whisper, ElevenLabs and Khaya AI (language and voice); Blender with BodyParts3D anatomy. Tested with 338 Python tests, 97 JavaScript tests and browser checks. Live at https://sentinel-cosmocare.vercel.app

WHAT WE CONSIDERED

Safety first: Sentinel describes changes from your normal and never diagnoses; it is not a medical device. Privacy: sensitive health fields are encrypted before they leave the device. Plus communication delay, offline operation, crew workload and keeping every number traceable to its source.
